[S., BHS dharma], dhamma denotes (an interpretation of) the essential nature and reality of existence and experience, the way things are: it is descriptive and prescriptive; it denotes also an essential attribute of men or animals; a quality or characteristic; Abh 784 (~o sabhāve pariyattipaññāñāyesu saccappakatīsu puññe ñeyye guṇācārasamādhisū pi nissattatāpattisu kāraṇādo); see also Sv 99,.3 foll., Ps I 17,.16 foll., It-a I 37,.20 foll., Paṭis-a 18,.1 foll., Bv-a 13,.4 foll., As 38,.23 foll. and Sadd 560,.25 foll.; — for Buddhists dhamma is used to denote an interlocking and interdependent assembly of concepts: the true nature of the world of experience, how that world works, and the way to transcend it, as understood by the Buddha; the progressive stages of understanding and nibbāna ; the behaviour, the practice, required to achieve understanding of the way the world of experience works, ie the way to reach arhatship, nibbāna ; the understanding and practice taught by the Buddha, the substance of his teaching, the texts of the Canon, especially the Suttapiṭaka ; all constituents of the world of experience, physical and mental, external and internal, progressively more and more minutely analysed; all constituents of prescribed practice, appropriate and beneficial actions; prescriptions for the members of the saṅgha ; — for people generally dhamma is an interpretation of the essential nature of existence and experience; the way one should act, depending on who one is, to maintain the way things are and should be; duty; right; justice; normative and beneficial actions; — 1. (i) how the world of experience works, the processes by which it works and is explained (especially as formulated in cattāri ariyasaccāni and paṭiccasamuppāda ), and the possibility and way of transcending it, as understood by the Buddha and taught by him (so that knowledge and understanding of it might bring enlightenment, arhatship, to others); Vin I 2,3* (yadā have pātubhavanti ~ā ātāpino jhāyato brāhmaṇassa ath’ assa kaṅkhā vapayanti sabbā yato pajānāti sahetudhammaṃ; Sp 954,.19 foll. : pātubhavantī ti uppajjanti ~ā ti anulomapaccayākārapaṭivedhasādhakā bodhipakkhiyadhammā, atha vā pātubhavantī ti pakāsenti abhisamayavasena vyattā pākaṭā honti, ~ā ti caturāriyasaccadhammā); 11,.2 (idaṃ dukkhaṃ ariyasaccan ti me bhikkhave pubbe ananussutesu ~esu cakkhuṃ udapādi); 12,.24 (ehi bhikkhū ti bhagavā avoca svākkhāto ~o cara brahmacariyaṃ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā ti); 15,.31 (idaṃ kho Yasa anupaddutaṃ idaṃ anupassaṭṭhaṃ ehi Yasa nisīda ~aṃ te desessāmī ti); 40,.19 foll. dhammapaṭisanthāra:
1dhamma
m. (and n.) [S., BHS dharma], dhamma denotes (an interpretation of) the essential nature and reality of existence and experience, the way things are: it is descriptive and prescriptive; it denotes also an essential attribute of men or animals; a quality or characteristic; Abh 784 (~o sabhāve pariyattipaññāñāyesu saccappakatīsu puññe ñeyye guṇācārasamādhisū pi nissattatāpattisu kāraṇādo); see also Sv 99,.3 foll., Ps I 17,.16 foll., It-a I 37,.20 foll., Paṭis-a 18,.1 foll., Bv-a 13,.4 foll., As 38,.23 foll. and Sadd 560,.25 foll.; — for Buddhists dhamma is used to denote an interlocking and interdependent assembly of concepts: the true nature of the world of experience, how that world works, and the way to transcend it, as understood by the Buddha; the progressive stages of understanding and nibbāna ; the behaviour, the practice, required to achieve understanding of the way the world of experience works, ie the way to reach arhatship, nibbāna ; the understanding and practice taught by the Buddha, the substance of his teaching, the texts of the Canon, especially the Suttapiṭaka ; all constituents of the world of experience, physical and mental, external and internal, progressively more and more minutely analysed; all constituents of prescribed practice, appropriate and beneficial actions; prescriptions for the members of the saṅgha ; — for people generally dhamma is an interpretation of the essential nature of existence and experience; the way one should act, depending on who one is, to maintain the way things are and should be; duty; right; justice; normative and beneficial actions; — 1. dhammānupassi:
1dhamma
m. (and n.) [S., BHS dharma], dhamma denotes (an interpretation of) the essential nature and reality of existence and experience, the way things are: it is descriptive and prescriptive; it denotes also an essential attribute of men or animals; a quality or characteristic; Abh 784 (~o sabhāve pariyattipaññāñāyesu saccappakatīsu puññe ñeyye guṇācārasamādhisū pi nissattatāpattisu kāraṇādo); see also Sv 99,.3 foll., Ps I 17,.16 foll., It-a I 37,.20 foll., Paṭis-a 18,.1 foll., Bv-a 13,.4 foll., As 38,.23 foll. and Sadd 560,.25 foll.; — for Buddhists dhamma is used to denote an interlocking and interdependent assembly of concepts: the true nature of the world of experience, how that world works, and the way to transcend it, as understood by the Buddha; the progressive stages of understanding and nibbāna ; the behaviour, the practice, required to achieve understanding of the way the world of experience works, ie the way to reach arhatship, nibbāna ; the understanding and practice taught by the Buddha, the substance of his teaching, the texts of the Canon, especially the Suttapiṭaka ; all constituents of the world of experience, physical and mental, external and internal, progressively more and more minutely analysed; all constituents of prescribed practice, appropriate and beneficial actions; prescriptions for the members of the saṅgha ; — for people generally dhamma is an interpretation of the essential nature of existence and experience; the way one should act, depending on who one is, to maintain the way things are and should be; duty; right; justice; normative and beneficial actions; — 1. 2kaṭhina
(in Be kathina), n. [BHS id.; cf AMg kaḍhina; Sp-ṭ (Be) III 335,.1 foll. : kathinan ti pañcānisaṃse anto-karaṇasamatthatāya thiran ti attho ti gaṇṭhipadesu vuttaṃ], 1. a framework (covered with a mat) to which the cloth for making robes was attached while being sewn; Vin II 116,.10 foll. (anujānāmi bhikkhave ~aṃ kaṭhinarajjuṃ tattha tattha obandhitvā cīvaraṃ sibbetun ti. visame ~aṃ pattharanti ~aṃ paribhijjati; Sp 1206,.7 : ~an ti nisseṇiṃ pi tattha attharitabbakaṭasārakakilañjānaṃ aññataraṃ pi); 117,.26 foll. (bhikkhū cīvaraṃ sibbetvā tatth’ eva ~aṃ ujjhitvā pakkamanti, undurehi pi upacikāhi pi khajjati … anujānāmi bhikkhave ~aṃ saṃharitun ti. ~aṃ paribhijjati, anujānāmi bhikkhave goghaṃsikāya ~aṃ saṃharitun ti ~aṃ viveṭhiyati …); — esp. kaṭhinaṃ attharati (i) spreads or covers the kaṭhina, ie makes a robe using the kaṭhina; — (ii) participates, at the end of the rains-residence, in a communal robe-making, during which certain rules and practices are suspended (perhaps in order to facilitate the robe-making); this involves a) a saṅghakamma allotting the material (and the use of the kaṭhina ) to a bhikkhu according to need and seniority; b) the preparation of the robe, by all the participating bhikkhu s, from washing the cloth to adding the kappabindu qv; c) the approval of the robe by one or more bhikkhu s. Only those can take part and share the privileges who have spent the earlier rain-retreat within that sīmā and have participated in the pavāraṇā ceremony. A minimum of five bhikkhu s is required, but unqualified ones may make up the number without sharing the privileges. The donor gives cloth, sewing materials and food to the participating bhikkhu s. The whole process must be completed in one day. cf Vin I 254,.25 foll. and Sp 1107,.10 foll.; Vin I 254,.8 (anujānāmi bhikkhave vassaṃ vutthānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ ~aṃ attharituṃ); 254,.19 (saṅgho imaṃ kaṭhinadussaṃ itthan-nāmassa bhikkhuno deti ~aṃ attharituṃ); M III 126,.10 (nābhijānāmi ~e cīvaraṃ sibbitā; Ps IV 193,.19 : ~e cīvaran ti kaṭhinacīvaraṃ, kaṭhinacīvaraṃ pi hi vassāvāsika-gatikam eva); Sp 1108,.10 (kaṭhinatthārasāṭakaṃ labhitvā suṭṭhu dhovitvā sūci-ādīni cīvarakammupakaraṇāni sajjetvā bahūhi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ tadaheva sibbitvā niṭṭhitasūcikammaṃ rajitvā kappabinduṃ datvā ~aṃ attharitabbaṃ); — (iii) displays the finished robe; Vin V 176,.22 foll.
